Where it began

Tristan Stubbs was born on 14 August 2000 in Knysna. He made his first-class debut for Eastern Province in January 2020, in the provincial three-day cup, and his one-day debut for the same side a month later. His first Twenty20 game came in February 2021, for the Warriors.

He has a Dutch passport too, and in 2021 he put it to good use, joining the Dutch club Excelsior '20 to play in the Topklasse.

The player

His big break came in May 2022, when Mumbai Indians added him to their IPL squad. Later that month South Africa picked him for a T20 series against India, and he made his international debut on 9 June 2022. His first one-day international followed in March 2023 against the West Indies, and in 2024 he made his first ODI hundred, against Ireland.

Test cricket arrived in January 2024, against India. It was a brisk start: he was out twice on the first day, something no debutant had done for 127 years. He soon found his feet. In October 2024 he made his first Test hundred, 106 against Bangladesh, and in 2025 he was part of the South Africa side that won the ICC World Test Championship.

By November 2026 he had played 15 Tests, scoring 792 runs at 30.46 with two hundreds, three fifties and a best of 122.

What made him special

Stubbs likes to take the game to the bowlers. In the 2024 IPL, playing for Delhi Capitals, he made 378 runs at a strike rate of 191. Delhi kept him for the next season, when he added another 300 runs. He bowls the odd off-break too, though by November 2026 his first Test wicket was a treat yet to come.

He fields well too. By November 2026 he had held 15 catches in his 15 Tests, a catch a match, which is the kind of steady return captains enjoy.

Away from the middle

His travels have taken him well beyond South Africa. As well as the Netherlands and the IPL, he played for the Jaffna Kings in the Lanka Premier League in 2022. He was in South Africa's squad for the 2024 T20 World Cup and for the 2025 Champions Trophy.

And finally

Being out twice on the first day of your Test career is not a record anyone sets out to win. Stubbs took it in good heart, and before the year was out he had a Test hundred to his name. It turned out the quickest way to the pavilion was also the start of a happy journey.
